resources.string: Installation, GitHub and Codex login, storage and reset
A persistent Arch Linux ARM environment on this phone. Shells share installed packages and files. Installation continues while you use other screens or apps. Android force-stop ends running programs.
Root filesystem: 168 MiB, plus starter packages and updates. Keep at least 4.3 GiB of internal storage free. Files stay in this app’s private storage.
Local Arch Linux requires an ARM64 Android device.
Downloading and verifying the Arch root filesystem…
Validating Arch Linux and initializing package signatures…

This deletes the entire local Linux filesystem, including your projects, installed packages, keys and configuration. This cannot be undone. Close all Local Arch shells first. Type DELETE ARCH to confirm.
This stops the local shell and its running programs. Your Arch files and installed packages remain available when you open a new Local Arch tab.

Installs or updates the latest stable Codex (with bubblewrap), Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, yay and herdr when you start setup. Fish is the default shell, with highlighting, suggestions and completion. Also includes Git, GitHub CLI, zoxide, search, editor, archive and build tools, Node 24 LTS and npm. System packages are fully updated; your projects and login credentials are preserved.
Installing starter tools and system updates…
Arch setup is running in the background…

Sign in here without typing terminal commands. Your phone browser opens for approval; return here to see the result. GitHub and Codex codes are copied for you. Credentials stay inside your private Arch environment. For Codex, first enable device code login in ChatGPT security settings (or ask your workspace admin).
Complete Claude Code sign-in in your phone browser, then return here. If the browser gives you a code instead of completing automatically, paste it below.
Ask which browser to use for Local Linux links
%1$s sign-in completed. Local Arch shells can now use this account.
Sign-in did not complete. Check your connection and device-login permissions, then retry. If a CLI was removed, reinstall the starter tools.
